title: What Does Done Even Mean? Agents and Paperclip's Liveness Model - Dotta, Paperclip
talk_summary: Dotta argues that 'done' is not a boolean but a bundle of claims (artifact, scope, rubric, evidence, verifier, authority, residual risk, next owner), and that agent systems must balance liveness (work keeps moving) against verification (work is checked) via a control plane with explicit state transitions, first-class blockers, reviewers/approvers, and watchdogs. Concrete advice: separate verifier from author (different model), require agents to produce evidence via tools (browser harness, screenshots), and enforce a clear chain of custody for the next step.

takeaways.technique: Separate verifier model from author model
takeaways.what_they_do: Route verification to a different model family than the one that produced the work, so the reviewer doesn't share the author's blind spots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Often, this means you're using a different model. So, if you're coding using Claude, have Codex verify.

takeaways.technique: Done as an object, not a boolean
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace a single 'done' checkbox with structured claims: artifact, scope, rubric/standard, evidence, verifier, approver authority, residual risk, and next action/owner.
takeaways.evidence_quote: stop treating done as a Boolean and treat it more like an object

takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents browser harnesses, screenshot tools, and hooks so they can actually exercise the artifact and attach proof rather than asserting completion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't just ask them to say, "Is this done?" But, give them the tools they need to verify that the work is done.

takeaways.technique: Watchdog / maximizer agent for goal completion
takeaways.what_they_do: A separate harness-agnostic agent is given a goal and enforces that all other agents keep working until the goal is achieved, rather than letting work stall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When you have a watchdog, it's another agent, um, who is given a goal, and it enforces that all of your agents continue to work until that goal has been achieved.

takeaways.technique: First-class blockers and explicit state transitions
takeaways.what_they_do: The control plane enforces allowed transitions per task and models blockers as first-class objects, so work can't enter invalid states or silently stall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have first-class blockers between tasks, and the control plane enforces those blockers.

takeaways.technique: Chain of custody for next owner
takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent is told explicitly who receives the work next, so handoffs are deterministic instead of the agent guessing or dropping the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Make sure you have a clear chain of custody, that every agent knows that as soon as they're done, who they're supposed to give the work to next.
